newsitem.title: UK: British government plans to privatize London subway.
newsitem.headline: British government plans to privatize London subway.

text.p: The British government wants to privatise London's underground railroad, the oldest subway system in the world and the transport lifeline of the capital, Transport Secretary George Young said Tuesday .
Young told BBC radio that he believed that the future of London Underground rested "in the private sector."
He said a proposal to sell off London Underground, popularly known as the Tube, will form a key part of the Conservative Party's campaign strategy for national elections that must be held by May 22.
The move would follow the privatisation of formerly state-run industries such as steel, railways, water, gas, electricity, telephone and coal.
The underground network, some of which dates back to 1865, comprises 248 stations on 11 lines that criss-cross one of Europe's biggest cities and transport 2.7 million people a day.

Young said privatisation would allow more money to be invested in the network and allow London Underground to plan for the long term and not compete for public funds with other government departments.
He said details of the sale had yet to be finalised.
